summary: Rabbi Hidary explores the Mishnaic rules for calculating the length of the lunar year and the number of full and deficient months allowed within it. He examines the debate between Rav Huna and Ula regarding the limits on these months and how they ensure the calendar remains aligned with the lunar cycle and public perception. The class also discusses the practical application of these rules, including how leap years and previous calendar adjustments influence the current year's calculations.
questions: Why is there a limit on how many months can have 30 days in a year?
What happens if the calendar calculation deviates significantly from the actual sighting of the moon?
How do the rabbis account for the extra days from a previous leap year when setting the current calendar?
Why does the timing of a Brit Milah sometimes shift beyond the eighth day?
How does the length of the lunar year affect the day of the week on which Rosh Hashanah falls?
